claim: The drone that hit a car in Lithuania on 18 October entered from Poland
evidence: Lithuanian radar track with a minute-by-minute timeline
conflict: Poland says its radars show no crossing. Ukraine says Russian jamming may have diverted it. Russian outlet EADaily spins it as Lithuania letting Ukrainian drones through.
verdict_note: Most likely a stray Ukrainian drone. Two NATO allies disagree on its route.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
conflict: Pentagon declined to comment but did not deny. Baltic ministries silent.
verdict_note: Credible but not confirmed on the record.

claim: Russia could make a limited attack on a NATO country in the coming months
claimed_by: Danish intelligence (25 September); US intelligence via WSJ and CNN (August)
conflict: Estonia's intelligence service: no intention to attack NATO this year. Putin: no plans to attack.
verdict_note: Services disagree on the odds but agree the risk is low and growing. Hybrid escalation is the more likely path.

claim: Russia is adding 16,000–20,000 military hospital beds near the Baltic states
claimed_by: Militarnyi, citing anonymous sources in Russian media; amplified by others
conflict: No official or imagery confirmation. Beds are also planned around Moscow and Smolensk, which fits Ukraine casualties.
verdict_note: Single source; headlines saying beds are moving 'close to the Baltics' overstate it.

claim: Belarus is preparing infrastructure for a Russian push to the Suwałki Gap by spring 2027
verdict_note: Plausible but partisan. Watch for imagery of rail and communications works.

claim: Ships at Baltiysk signal a Kaliningrad build-up for an attack
evidence: Imagery shows equipment being loaded out
conflict: OSINT analysts and Militarnyi: destination unknown; the same ships have supplied Africa before.
verdict_note: The imagery is real; the framing is not supported by it.

claim: NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade of Kaliningrad
claimed_by: Russian embassies and a diplomatic note to NATO (late September)
conflict: NATO replied that none of its exercises threaten Russian territory.
verdict_note: No evidence offered. Reads as a pretext narrative backing nuclear warnings.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
conflict: Estonia's foreign minister: no official US proposal. Estonia's PM: allies are asking Estonia to hold back. Peskov: reports should be taken with a grain of salt. Pentagon declines to comment. Lithuania and Latvia silent.
verdict_note: Still unconfirmed on the record, but Estonian reactions suggest informal pressure rather than a formal request.

claim: Russian intelligence was behind the Starlink arson attacks in Poland, Bulgaria and Lithuania
claimed_by: Poland's intelligence minister; Lithuania's prime minister; Der Spiegel
evidence: Official statements; arrests in four countries; press reports on the gang leader's protection in Russia
conflict: Lithuanian police say the ultimate motive has not been established. German broadcaster ARD notes that gang membership is hard to establish. Russia routinely denies such accusations.
verdict_note: The cross-border link is official; the Russian tasking is asserted by officials but not yet shown in court.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
conflict: Not announced by the Kremlin. The Kremlin ruled out European participation in the Abu Dhabi round on 29 October, while the report says Moscow wants Europeans at the table.
verdict_note: Plausible given Russia's 2021 demands, but a single anonymous-source report.

claim: The Kaliningrad blackout was caused by a protection system tripping at the CHP-2 power plant
claimed_by: Kaliningrad regional authorities; grid operator Rosseti
conflict: Ukrainian outlets say the cause could not be verified; social media posts speculated about sabotage without evidence.
verdict_note: The official explanation is plausible and not contradicted by any evidence, but it has not been independently verified.

claim: Russia does not want a war with Europe
conflict: Danish and US intelligence see a low but growing risk of a limited test of NATO; European officials blame Russia for an ongoing sabotage campaign.
verdict_note: Statements of intent cannot be verified; the hybrid record runs against the reassurance.

claim: Belarus is relaying signals for Russian attack drones
claimed_by: Ukraine's border guard spokesperson and military intelligence chief; Ukrainian monitoring project E-radar
conflict: Minsk has not responded. No NATO or Lithuanian technical body has confirmed it. Ukrainian explanations (commercial LTE networks or purpose-built relays) differ.
verdict_note: Relevant to the Baltics because a Russian Gerbera drone was shot down over Lithuania in September; all sources are Ukrainian or Belarusian opposition.

claim: The US is pressing Lithuania to allow Belarusian potash transit despite EU sanctions
conflict: Lithuanian PM said in September no US request had been received. The State Department did not respond. Lithuanian officials reject the idea on the record.
verdict_note: Consistent with earlier reporting of US outreach to Minsk; the request itself is not on the record.
